newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM awards Aboriginal mine contract.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM awards Aboriginal mine contract.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Thursday it awarded a contract to an Aboriginal-run joint venture to transport copper and gold concentrates 160 km from the Ernest Henry mine in Queensland to Mount Isa for smelting.
The five-year multi-million dollar contract was awarded to a partnership of the Koutha Aboriginal Development Corp Ltd and Gulf Transportation Co Pty Ltd, an MIM spokesman said.
MIM holds a 51 percent interest in the mine. Savage Resources Ltd owns the remaining 49 percent.

"Koutha was established and is run by Aboriginal people as a self-help mechanism to create jobs and other economic benefits for Aboriginal people in the region," MIM and Savage said in a joint statement.
The A$350 million Ernest Henry project is designed to produce at a maximum rate of 350,000 tonnes of concentrate annually, containing 95,000 tonnes of copper and 120,000 ounces of gold.
Concentrate haulage from the mine is expected to commence in the third quarter of 1997, the statement said.
